contents.text: Mean and median are measures of center.

elements.text: The mean is calculated by taking the average of all the values in a data set.
The median is found by ordering the values in a data set from least to greatest, then selecting the middle value.

contents.text: Standard deviation and interquartile range (IQR) are measures of variation.

elements.text: The standard deviation measures how much data values typically vary from the mean.
The IQR is the range of the middle 50% of the data set.

contents.text: The mean and standard deviation can be strongly affected by the shape of a distribution and by outliers. So, they are appropriate measures for symmetric distributions but may not be appropriate for skewed distributions or when there are outliers.

Since the median is the middle value in a data set, it is less affected by the shape of a distribution or by outliers. And, since the IQR is the range of the middle 50% of the data set, it is also less affected by the shape or by outliers. So, they are almost always appropriate measures.
